topic: What if dinosaurs never went extinct? Scientists think mammals, and maybe humans, might never have become dominant.

episode.title: What If Dinosaurs Never Went Extinct?

shots.narration: What if dinosaurs never went extinct?
shots.scene: Colourful 3D animated laboratory, vertical frame, glowing dinosaur hologram above a round projector, no text.
shots.action: nova presents the towering dinosaur hologram to byte.

shots.narration: An asteroid impact helped drive non-bird dinosaurs to extinction.
shots.scene: Colourful laboratory with a holographic prehistoric Earth and an approaching asteroid, no text.
shots.action: nova traces the asteroid's path toward the holographic Earth.
shots.mood: Dramatic violet lighting, thoughtful scientific discovery.

shots.narration: [excited] Afterward, mammals diversified into many newly available ecological roles.
shots.scene: Laboratory hologram showing a lush forest with small climbing, burrowing and grazing mammals, no text.
shots.action: nova expands the hologram into a varied mammal-filled landscape.

shots.narration: Scientists think surviving dinosaurs might have kept dominating land ecosystems.
shots.scene: Colourful laboratory with a hypothetical holographic landscape of large dinosaurs and small mammals, no text.
shots.action: nova replaces the mammal-filled landscape with the dinosaur-filled alternative.
shots.mood: Sunlit greens, immense scale, curious possibility.

shots.narration: Scientists think mammals might have faced stronger competition for resources.
shots.scene: Laboratory hologram close-up of a small mammal beside a plant-eating dinosaur beneath fruiting vegetation, no text.
shots.action: The holographic dinosaur eats foliage above the small mammal.
shots.mood: Gentle daylight, peaceful but crowded habitat.

shots.narration: [whispers] Scientists think mammals might never have become dominant.
shots.scene: Laboratory with a tall holographic forest, large dinosaurs in clearings and tiny mammals beneath roots, no text.
shots.action: nova magnifies a tiny mammal's sheltered corner of the hologram.
shots.mood: Soft amber glow, intimate scientific curiosity.

shots.narration: Scientists think humans might never have become dominant either.
shots.scene: Colourful laboratory with a holographic dinosaur landscape and a separate translucent modern city model, no text.
shots.action: nova fades the hypothetical city model away.

shots.narration: Evolution follows changing environments, not a plan to produce humans.
shots.scene: Laboratory hologram resembling a branching tree with animal silhouettes at different branch tips, no text.
shots.action: nova spreads the holographic branches outward in many directions.

shots.narration: [surprised] Birds are dinosaurs—what if humans could fly?
shots.scene: Bright 3D laboratory with a feathered dinosaur hologram beside a modern bird hologram, no text.
shots.action: The holographic bird spreads its wings above nova and byte.
shots.mood: Golden light, joyful revelation and anticipation.

episode.description: Dr. Nova shows Byte a world where non-bird dinosaurs survived. Explore why scientists think mammals—and perhaps humans—might never have become dominant, plus the dinosaurs still living today.
